entry.title: Quark's Outlines: Python Name Spaces
entry.summary:
Quark’s Outlines: Python Name Spaces
Overview, Historical Timeline, Problems & Solutions When you write code in Python, you give names to values. A Python name space is the place where those names are stored. It is like a labeled shelf that holds objects. When you ask for a name, Python looks in the shelf to find it. A name space is a mapping between names and objects. In Python, that mapping is usually a dictionary. Each name space stores the current known names and their values. Python lets you manage names by storing them in name spaces. x = 5 print(globals()["x"]) # prints: # 5
The globals() function returns the current global name space. You can look up a name and find its value. Python uses three main name spaces when running code: local, global, and built-in. Each one is searched…
